newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes strong on U.S. long bond yield.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes strong on U.S. long bond yield.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed sharply firmer against the dollar on Monday.
Traders said foreign investors stepped into Mexican financial markets and local dealers sold long dollar positions spurred by falling yields on the U.S. long bond.
"The (local) market had been very long on dollars since last week, and they let go at this level," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 4.7 and 4.8 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.8950/7.8990 and 7.8920/7.8950 per dollar.
This was the first time 48-hour contracts had closed firmer than 7.90 per dollar since March 25.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 4.5 centavos weaker at 7.8950/7.8980 per dollar.
Overnight funding rates on Cetes were down 50 basis points to 23.00 percent in late trade due on demand for paper from foreign investors.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was up 14/32 to yield 7.08 percent.
"Foreign brokers have been stepping into Mexico since Friday, mainly the money market," another trader said.
Traders said dollars were in supply due to a favorable outlook for inflation data expected from Banco de Mexico on Wednesday.
A Reuters survey MXAAP of Mexico City financial houses showed they forecast an average rise of 1.31 percent for consumer prices in March, compared to 1.68 percent in February.

Nonetheless, traders said the peso could relinquish ground gained in the coming days on demand for dollars from dealers hedging against U.S. producer price data on Friday, and the prospect of higher yields on U.S. long bonds.
Dealers said possible falls in domestic primary interest rates on Tuesday could also fuel demand for dollars.
